steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' library.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and hooks
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are imported, enabling component creation and state management.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState, which are essential for building React components with state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported React, but don't forget to also import the useState hook. Both are needed for this lesson.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are not correct. You need to import both React and useState from the 'react' library.

steps.title: Create the StaffPatterns component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named StaffPatterns that will serve as the main container for the lesson content.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function with the name StaffPatterns that returns JSX.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the StaffPatterns component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named StaffPatterns is defined, ready to hold the lesson content.
successCriteria: The component StaffPatterns is defined as a function or arrow function and returns JSX (or null).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main StaffPatterns component. This will be the container for all our patterns content.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've defined a function or arrow function named StaffPatterns that returns something (like null or JSX).
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined yet. Create a functional component named StaffPatterns that returns JSX (or null for now).

steps.title: Initialize state for selected pattern
steps.instruction: Inside the StaffPatterns component, initialize a state variable called 'selectedPattern' using useState with an initial value of null.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The state variable should track which staff engineer pattern is currently selected.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: state initialization for a selected item
const [selectedItem, setSelectedItem] = useState(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'selectedPattern' initialized to null, ready to track the selected staff engineer pattern.
successCriteria: The component contains a useState call that declares 'selectedPattern' with initial value null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized state to track the selected staff engineer pattern.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState to declare a variable called 'selectedPattern' with initial value null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization isn't quite right. Remember to use useState to create a 'selectedPattern' variable starting as null.

steps.title: Define pattern data structure
steps.instruction: Inside the StaffPatterns component, define a constant array named 'patterns' that contains objects representing staff engineer patterns. Each object should have properties: id, name, description, and keyPrinciples.
steps.hint: Create an array of objects with the specified properties. Use descriptive values for each pattern.
steps.expectedOutcome: The patterns array is defined with at least one pattern object containing the required properties.
successCriteria: A 'patterns' array is defined with objects containing id, name, description, and keyPrinciples properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the pattern data structure with all required properties.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined an array, but make sure each pattern object has id, name, description, and keyPrinciples properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The patterns array is not defined correctly. Ensure you create an array of objects with the specified properties.

steps.title: Create pattern selection handler
steps.instruction: Define a function called handlePatternSelect inside your StaffPatterns component that takes a pattern ID parameter and updates the selectedPattern state with that ID.
steps.hint: Create a function that accepts an id parameter and calls setSelectedPattern with that id.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handlePatternSelect function is defined that updates the selectedPattern state when called with a pattern ID.
successCriteria: The handlePatternSelect function is defined, takes an id parameter, and calls setSelectedPattern with that id.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the pattern selection handler function. This function will be used to update which staff engineer pattern is currently selected.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function takes an id parameter and calls setSelectedPattern with that parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handler function isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a function called handlePatternSelect that accepts a pattern ID and updates the state.

steps.title: Create pattern clearing handler
steps.instruction: Define a function called handleClearSelection inside your StaffPatterns component that resets the selectedPattern state to null.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setSelectedPattern with null as the argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a handleClearSelection function that can be called to clear the selected pattern.
successCriteria: The handleClearSelection function is defined and calls setSelectedPattern(null).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the clearing handler. This function will allow users to deselect any pattern.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function is named handleClearSelection and it calls setSelectedPattern(null).
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a function called handleClearSelection that sets selectedPattern to null.

steps.title: Add main container structure
steps.instruction: In your StaffPatterns component, return a main container div with the class name 'staff-patterns-container'.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement with a div element that has the specified class name.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a div element with the class 'staff-patterns-container', establishing the basic layout structure.
successCriteria: The component returns a div element with className='staff-patterns-container'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main container structure for the Staff Patterns component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning a div element with the exact class name 'staff-patterns-container'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a div element with className='staff-patterns-container'. Check your return statement.

steps.title: Add header and introduction
steps.instruction: Inside the StaffPatterns component's return statement, add a header element with the lesson title 'Staff Engineer Patterns' and a brief introductory paragraph explaining what staff engineer patterns are.
steps.hint:
You can use an

for the title and a

for the introductory paragraph. Place them inside the return statement.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display a header with the lesson title and an introductory paragraph about staff engineer patterns.
successCriteria:
The return statement includes an

with the text 'Staff Engineer Patterns' and a

with introductory text about staff engineer patterns.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a clear header and introduction that provides context about staff engineer patterns.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some structure, but make sure to include both the header and introductory paragraph with appropriate content.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The header and introduction are missing or incomplete. Add an

with the lesson title and a

with introductory text.

steps.title: Create pattern list display
steps.instruction: Inside the component's return statement, map through the pattern data to create clickable list items, wiring each onClick to the handlePatternSelect function.
steps.hint: Use the patternData array to generate list items. Each item should have an onClick handler that calls handlePatternSelect with the pattern's id.
steps.expectedOutcome: A list of clickable pattern items appears in the UI, each triggering the selection handler when clicked.
successCriteria: patternData is mapped to create list items
each list item has an onClick handler calling handlePatternSelect
each list item displays the pattern name
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a clickable list of staff engineer patterns. Each pattern can now be selected by clicking on it.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've made progress with the pattern list. Make sure each list item has an onClick handler that calls handlePatternSelect with the pattern's id.
steps.feedbackWrong: The pattern list isn't displaying correctly. You need to map through patternData to create list items with onClick handlers that call handlePatternSelect.

steps.title: Add pattern detail display and clear button
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add conditional rendering to display the selected pattern's details when available, and include a clear button wired to handleClearSelection.
steps.hint: Use a ternary operator to check if selectedPattern exists, then find the matching pattern from patternData to display its name and description. Add a button with onClick that calls handleClearSelection.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display detailed information about the selected staff engineer pattern when one is chosen, and provide a button to clear the selection.
successCriteria: Selected pattern details are conditionally rendered using a ternary operator, the matching pattern is found from patternData, and a clear button with onClick={handleClearSelection} is included.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented conditional rendering for pattern details and added a clear button. This completes the interactive pattern explorer.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using a ternary operator to conditionally render the details, finding the matching pattern from patternData, and wiring the clear button to handleClearSelection.
steps.feedbackWrong: The implementation doesn't match the requirements. You need to add conditional rendering for selected pattern details and a clear button wired to the handler.
